title: Positive-copy relative Proj recovers an affine morphism
statement:
Let $h:T\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and assume explicitly that $\mathcal E=h_*\mathcal O_T$, with its natural commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebra structure, is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Let $\mathcal B$ be the graded sheaf algebra with $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$, $\mathcal B_n=\mathcal E$ for $n>0$, positive multiplication $a[m]b[n]=(ab)[m+n]$, and degree-zero action through the algebra structure, as in [lem-trf-positive-copy-graded-quotient]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism over $S$
$$\theta:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T,$$
with relative Proj as in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. More precisely, on every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, write $h^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $C=R\oplus\bigoplus_{n\geq1}A[n]$ with the above multiplication, and put $t=1_A[1]$. The whole scheme $\operatorname{Proj}C$ is its standard open $D_+(t)$ [def-pc-proj]. There is an $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$C_{(t),0}\xrightarrow{\sim}A,\qquad a[m]/t^m\longmapsto a\quad(m\geq1),$$
with inverse $a\mapsto a[1]/t$, using the degree-zero homogeneous localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. The restriction of $\theta$ is the standard-chart isomorphism followed by the spectrum map of this inverse ring isomorphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These local isomorphisms and their inverses commute with inclusions of affine opens, including on affine refinements of overlaps, and determine $\theta$ uniquely. The statements include $A=0$, noninjective $R\to A$, and arbitrary non-Noetherian bases; $h$ need not be finite.

proof.text: Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)$ and write $\pi:P\to S$. The construction in [lem-trf-positive-copy-graded-quotient], applied to the assumed quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal E$, makes $\mathcal B$ quasi-coherent and identifies its affine section algebras, compatibly with affine restriction. Thus [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] applies and supplies $i_V:\pi^{-1}(V)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}C$ compatible with further restriction. By [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $h^{-1}(V)$ is affine; use its section ring $A$. The equality $\mathcal E(V)=\Gamma(h^{-1}(V),\mathcal O_T)=A$ is the definition of direct image, so its section algebra is exactly the $C$ in the statement, not an algebra requiring an additional comparison.

source.place: Tags 01NQ (constructions-lemma-glue-relative-proj) and 01NO (constructions-lemma-proj-inclusion); apply the positive-copy construction to the algebra in Tag 0B3I.

proof.text: Fix such $V$ and put $t=1_A[1]$. For every $a\in A$ and $n\geq1$, multiplication gives $(a[n])^2=t(a^2)[2n-1]$. If a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ contains $t$, it therefore contains every $a[n]$, hence the irrelevant ideal $C_+$, because its elements are finite sums of positive homogeneous elements. This excludes $\mathfrak p$ from Proj by [def-pc-proj]. Every point of $\operatorname{Proj}C$ consequently belongs to $D_+(t)$. This open is the entire open subscheme, not merely a subset with the same closed points.

source.place: Tags 01M4 (constructions-lemma-standard-open), 01MB (constructions-lemma-proj-scheme); elementary homogeneous-prime calculation for this C.

proof.text: Write $L=C_{(t),0}$. By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], a fraction has numerator in degree equal to its denominator exponent. Its exponent can be made positive by multiplying numerator and denominator by $t$: for degree-zero numerator $r$, the fraction relation gives $r/1=(rt)/t=\iota(r)[1]/t$, where $\iota:R\to A$ is the structure map. This equality uses $rt=\iota(r)[1]$, not cancellation by $t$. Hence every element is $a[m]/t^m$ with $m\geq1$. The equality relation in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] says that two such representatives, $a[m]/t^m$ and $b[n]/t^n$, are equal precisely when some $k\geq0$ kills their cross difference. That difference after multiplication by $t^k$ is $(a-b)[m+n+k]$. This lies in a positive-degree copy of $A$, so it is zero precisely when $a=b$. Conversely, $a=b$ already makes the cross difference zero. Thus the assignment $\alpha_V(a[m]/t^m)=a$ is well-defined and injective, with no use of injectivity of $\iota$.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (constructions-lemma-standard-open), degree-zero chart ring; fraction equality is Algebra Tag 00CO (algebra-definition-localization).

proof.text:
The fraction operations in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] give
$$\frac{a[m]}{t^m}+\frac{b[n]}{t^n}=\frac{(a+b)[m+n]}{t^{m+n}},\qquad \frac{a[m]}{t^m}\frac{b[n]}{t^n}=\frac{ab[m+n]}{t^{m+n}}.$$
The unit is $t/t$, and the image of $r\in R$ is $\iota(r)[1]/t$. Therefore $\alpha_V:L\to A$ preserves addition, multiplication, the unit and the $R$-algebra structure. Every $a$ is the image of $a[1]/t$. Moreover $a[m]/t^m=a[1]/t$ by the equality calculation in Step 3. It follows that $\beta_V(a)=a[1]/t$ is the inverse $R$-algebra isomorphism. This proves both requested formulas including the degree-zero structural map. If $A=0$, then $t=0$, so localizing at $t$ gives $L=0$; both displayed maps are the unique maps of zero rings. Thus the argument includes the empty affine scheme without requiring $t$ to be nonzero.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (constructions-lemma-standard-open); explicit fraction operations using Algebra Tag 00CO (algebra-definition-localization).

proof.text: Since $t$ is homogeneous of degree one, [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] gives the standard-chart isomorphism $j_V:D_+(t)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$. By Step 2 its source is all of $\operatorname{Proj}C$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\beta_V):\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha_V)$. Set $\theta_V=\operatorname{Spec}(\beta_V)\circ j_V\circ i_V:\pi^{-1}(V)\simeq h^{-1}(V)$. It is over $V$: on the chart the structural map of [def-nagata-affine-proj] is induced by $R\to L$, $r\mapsto r/1$, and Step 4 sends this to $\iota(r)$. Functoriality of Spec identifies its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the given restriction of $h$.

source.place: Tags 01MB (constructions-lemma-proj-scheme) and 01M4 (constructions-lemma-standard-open), the standard chart and its degree-zero structural map.

proof.text:
For affine opens $W\subseteq V$, let $u:R\to R'$ and $v:A\to A'$ be the section restrictions. The compatibility clause of [lem-trf-positive-copy-graded-quotient] makes the graded restriction $r\mapsto u(r)$ in degree zero and $a[n]\mapsto v(a)[n]$ in positive degree; it sends $t$ to $t'=1_{A'}[1]$. By the specified chart restrictions of [def-nagata-relative-proj], the induced chart-ring map is
$$\ell_{VW}:L\to L',\qquad a[m]/t^m\mapsto v(a)[m]/(t')^m.$$
For each representative, $\alpha_W\ell_{VW}(a[m]/t^m)=v(a)=v\alpha_V(a[m]/t^m)$ and $\ell_{VW}\beta_V(a)=v(a)[1]/t'=\beta_Wv(a)$. These are equalities on every element by Step 3. Applying the functorial Spec construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum] proves that both $\theta_V$ and $\theta_V^{-1}$ commute with restriction to $W$. The actual inclusion $h^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow h^{-1}(V)$ induces $v$ on sections, so the square compares the required morphisms, not just abstract affine schemes.

source.place: Tags 01NO (constructions-lemma-proj-inclusion) and 01NQ (constructions-lemma-glue-relative-proj); explicit equality of the two coefficient-restriction maps.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], affine opens cover $S$, and every overlap $V\cap V'$ admits an affine open covering $(W_a)$. Each $W_a$ is contained in both $V$ and $V'$. Step 6 makes $\theta_V$ and $\theta_{V'}$ restrict to $\theta_{W_a}$ on $\pi^{-1}(W_a)$; these preimages cover $\pi^{-1}(V\cap V')$. The equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] proves equality of the two maps to $T$ on that overlap. The same argument on $h^{-1}(W_a)$ gives overlap equality of the inverse maps to $P$. Applying its existence clause twice glues them to $\theta:P\to T$ and $\eta:T\to P$. On each $\pi^{-1}(V)$ the composite $\eta\theta$ is $\theta_V^{-1}\theta_V=1$, and on each $h^{-1}(V)$ the composite $\theta\eta$ is $\theta_V\theta_V^{-1}=1$; its equality clause makes these identities global. It also shows $h\theta=\pi$, since this holds on every $\pi^{-1}(V)$, and gives uniqueness with the prescribed local formulas. No affine-intersection, finite-generation, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis has entered.
